Furthermore, we analyzed the nucleotide identity ( Supplementary Figure 3 ) and key amino acid mutation sites ( Supplementary Table 1–3 ) of the three capsid proteins. High within-variant identity was identified (exceeding 99.800%), while notable differences were identified between variants. For the penton base gene, the 7 V variant exhibited relatively low sequence identity (98.070–98.310%) compared to other variants. It contained 7 mutation sites relative to the prototype 7p, and 4–5 mutations when compared to the other two circulating variants. In the hypervariable region (HVR), the 7 V variant carried an I158 T mutation. Within the RGD region, the 7 V variant showed a Q338H mutation, the 7E1 variant exhibited a E320 V mutation, and the majority of 7E2 variants featured a D325N mutation ( Supplementary Table 1) . The hexon gene exhibited the greatest divergence, with identity between the 7p prototype and the other three variants ranging from 97.350% to 97.460%. These differences were primarily localized in HVR1 (7 sites) and HVR7 (12 sites) ( Supplementary Table 2 ). In contrast, the 7 V variant showed high identity (99.730–99.750%) with the other two circulating variants, indicating strong conservation among all currently prevalent HAdV-7 isolates except the three prototype strains. Given that the hexon protein is a major target for neutralizing antibodies, these results suggest that U.S. military HAdV-7 vaccines developed based on the 7 V variant are still functional in protection against the prevalent 7E1 and 7E2 variants. In the case of the fibre protein, the 7p prototype demonstrated considerable divergence from the other three variants (98.710–99.010%), featuring 2–3 mutations in the tail region and 1–3 mutations in the knob domain (Supplementary Table 3) . The differences among the other three variants were less than 0.600%. These findings suggest that currently prevalent HAdV-7 isolates do not exhibit significant fibre diversity. However, certain mutations in the knob coding region between the prototype and circulating isolates – such as T142R (present in 7 V, 7E1, and 7E2 variants), I147 V (found in a subset of 7E2 variant) and I273 T (7E1 variant) – may influence receptor interaction and potentially alter viral adsorption efficiency. Based on amino acid mutation analysis, a number of unique background mutation sites were identified in HAdV-7E1 or HAdV-7E2 variants. This suggests that HAdV-7E1 and HAdV-7E2 variants evolved independently from the prototype strain. Over the course of their circulation, the prevalence of these two variants in the human population has shifted, with HAdV-7E2 currently becoming the predominant variant. Evolutionary divergence times of HAdV-7 Using the Bayesian-MCMC method, we performed a whole-genome analysis of HAdV-7 isolates from five countries – China (200 isolates), the United States (81 isolates), Russia (3 isolates), Japan (1 isolate), and Germany (1 isolate) – to reconstruct the temporal dynamics, estimate the mean nucleotide substitution rate, infer the time to the most recent common ancestor (tMRCA), and investigate evolutionary divergence. The average nucleotide substitution rate of HAdV-7 was found to be 3.89 × 10 −5 mutations/site/year (95% HPD: 3.05–4.76 × 10 −5 ). The tMRCA was estimated to have occurred in 1821 (95% HPD: 1717-1891), marking the first evolutionary divergence that separated the HAdV-7 prototype from other isolates. The second divergence occurred in 1907 (95% HPD: 1870-1933), resulting in the separation of the HAdV-7 V and HAdV-7E variants. The third divergence emerged in 1978 (95% HPD: 1964-1987), dividing the HAdV-7E variant into the HAdV-7E1 and HAdV-7E2 variants ( Figure 7 ). The estimated timing of all major divergence events suggests a pattern of periodic emergence. Accordingly, these findings indicate that a new variant of HAdV-7 emerges approximately every 70–80 years. Figure 7. Bayesian estimation of the time to the most recent common ancestor for HAdV-7. The average nucleotide substitution rate of HAdV-7 was calculated at 3.89 × 10 −5 mutations/site/year (95% HPD: 3.05–4.76 × 10 −5 ). The most recent common ancestor is estimated to have appeared in 1821 (95% HPD: 1717-1891), while the most recent 7E2 variant ancestor emerged in 1978 (95% HPD: 1964–1987). Discussion It has been 70 years since Berge et al. [ 38 ] first identified HAdV-7 in 1954. We conducted a meta-analysis of global HAdV-7 infections from 1954 to 2023, revealing a steady increase in reported cases and literature over time ( Figure 2 ). Notably, 40.00% of reports were published in the last decade, with 66.75% focusing on civilian cases. The incidence of HAdV-7 infections has risen steadily, with military-related infections surging; 58.23% of cases were reported in the past 10 years. Additionally, the number of civilian infections reported in the decade since 2014 was 3.4 times greater than that of the previous decade ( Figure 3 a), indicating that HAdV-7 infections are prevalent in both military and civilian populations and may be on the rise. This phenomenon may be attributed to improved diagnostic capabilities and increased public health awareness. In patients infected with HAdV-7, we observed that children (56.75%) and military personnel (35.06%) constituted the primary susceptible groups, accounting for 91.81% of cases with documented age information. Additionally, the number of male infected individuals (4,484 cases) was 3.21 times higher than that of females (1,396 cases), which aligns with the clinical findings reported by Wei et al. [ 4 , 39 , 40 ], collectively indicating a higher susceptibility to HAdV-7 among males. Furthermore, in a study involving intravenous injection of mice with a high dose of HAdV-5, male mice exhibited more severe pathological damage and significantly higher fatality compared to females [ 41 ]. These results suggest that HAdV infection may lead to more severe clinical outcomes, including a higher risk of fatality, in males. HAdV-7 cases have been reported on all continents except Antarctica, with Asia exhibiting the highest incidence, particularly in Mainland China. This contrasts with the global epidemic trend of HAdV-4 infections between 1960 and 2020, as studied by Coleman et al. [ 42 ]. The majority of HAdV-4 infection cases (21,130 cases, 86.14%) occurred in North America, primarily concentrated in the United States (21,124 cases, 86.12%), while Asia accounted for only 7.05%. Among these, the number of HAdV-4 cases reported in Mainland China was 147, representing just 0.60% of the total infections. This phenomenon is likely attributable to the U.S. military’s vaccination strategy. Routine HAdV-4 and HAdV-7 vaccinations for military recruits, implemented in 1971, drastically reduced infections. However, following their discontinuation in 1997, HAdV-4 resurged, while HAdV-7 infections increased only slightly, [ 12 , 43–45 ]. To our knowledge, no systematic retrospective studies have been conducted on other HAdV types. However, HAdV-3 infections have exhibited varying prevalence rates globally: South Korea (1990–1998, 15%; 1991–2007, 37%; 2010, 74.3%) [ 46–48 ]; Mainland China (1976–1980, 39.08%; 2006–2008, 43.48%; 2009–2012, 37.3%) [ 49–51 ]. These variations underscore the influence of specific HAdV types, vaccination status, and regional factors on infection patterns. Investigating HAdV-specific infections by time and region can help inform vaccine interventions aimed at reducing morbidity and fatality. Different types of HAdV present varying manifestations and severity. Among them, HAdV-7 is highly pathogenic, often resulting in severe outcomes, including death, with the CFR of 2.41%. This rate is significantly higher than that of HAdV-4 (0.11%) [ 42 ]. This suggests that HAdV-7 infections are more severe. Deaths from HAdV-7 have been reported in 26 countries, with encephalitis being a notable complication, as highlighted by Gerber et al [ 29 ]. In contrast, HAdV-4 fatalities were primarily due to respiratory complications, with only one case of encephalitis reported [ 52 ]. We also found that among the distribution of HAdV genotypes associated with fatalities, HAdV-7 accounted for the highest proportion (262 cases, 39.28%). Phylogenetic analysis of 313 HAdV-7 genomes revealed four clusters: HAdV-7 prototype, HAdV-7 V, and HAdV-7E variants, with HAdV-7E further divided into HAdV-7E1 and HAdV-7E2. This classification corresponds approximately with the branches of the whole genome phylogenetic tree previously constructed by Duan et al. [ 53 ]. Based on strains isolated at different times, Duan et al. classified HAdV-7E1 and HAdV-7E2 variants into one cluster. Since 2005, HAdV-7E2 has emerged as the dominant strain globally. Phylogenetic analysis of capsid protein genes indicated that the penton base gene aligns with whole-genome phylogeny, while hexon and fibre genes exhibit distinct clustering patterns. The results of the phylogenetic analysis of a single capsid protein gene are consistent with earlier findings by Li et al. [ 15 , 54–56 ], who classified HAdV-7 into more than 20 genotypes using restriction endonuclease analysis, although this classification did not fully reflect the complete evolutionary characteristics of HAdV-7. For instance, ak38 ( JX423386.1 , from 2003), previously classified as HAdV-7 h, has a higher sequence identity with HAdV-3 and was retyped as HAdV-B66 in 2012 [ 20 ]. Amino acid mutations identified across HAdV-7 variants may alter the spatial conformation of capsid proteins, potentially impacting their biological functions. The knob domain of the adenovirus fibre protein is critical for determining receptor tropism. Notably, the recombinant adenovirus HAdV-D64 acquired its fibre gene from HAdV-D37, which enabled it to infect human corneal epithelial cells and induce significantly stronger corneal inflammation compared to its parental strains [ 57 ]. Species C adenoviruses like HAdV-5 interact with the CAR receptor through apical residues such as Ser408, Pro409, Tyr477 and Leu485 [ 58 ]. HAdV Species B, such as HAdV-7, bind to DSG2 via an extended lateral surface, with key residues including Asn190, Asn192, Asp265, Phe269, and Val300. Mutations at these sites – such as D265A and F269A – have been shown to significantly reduce receptor-binding affinity [ 59 , 60 ]. While HAdV-11 utilizes an “arginine switch” (Arg279-Arg280) for high-affinity binding to CD46, HAdV-7 contains Gln279 at the equivalent position, resulting in only low-affinity, non-functional interaction with CD46 [ 61 ]. In our study, all HAdV-7 strains analyzed retained Gln279 in the fibre knob. However, we identified novel mutations in the knob domain of HAdV-7 variants compared to the HAdV-7p prototype, including T142R (present in HAdV-7 V, 7E1, and 7E2 variants), I147 V (found in some HAdV-7E2 strains), and I273 T (identified in the HAdV-7E1 variant) ( Supplementary Table 3 ). Whether these mutations influence receptor-binding affinity among different HAdV-7 variants requires further investigation. The hypervariable regions (HVRs) of the hexon represent the primary targets of neutralizing antibodies, and their antigenic diversity drives immune evasion [ 62 ]. Intertypic recombination of hexon genes can lead to dramatic antigenic shifts, as seen in the emergence of HAdV-B55 [ 63 ]. Additionally, frequent recombination or point mutations among hexons can result in antigenic drift, exemplified by HAdV-D53 [ 64 ]. Beyond recombination, HVR point mutations can also alter immune recognition via interactions with host factors. For instance, residues in HVR7 of HAdV-5 (I421, T423, E424, T425, and E451) form a binding site for coagulation factor X (FX); FX binding shields neutralizing epitopes and redirects the virus to hepatocytes. Replacing the HVR7 of HAdV-5 with that of HAdV-26, or introducing mutations such as I421G, T423N, E424S, L426Y, and E451Q, completely abolishes the FX-mediated effects in vitro [ 65 ]. In this study, HAdV-7 variants exhibited high similarity among themselves (99.730% to 99.810%), yet showed substantial divergence from the prototype strain (97.350% to 97.460%) ( Supplementary Figure 3 ), with mutations predominantly concentrated in HVR1 and HVR7 (Supplementary Table 2 ). These alterations may disrupt antibody recognition by modifying epitope conformation or mimicking FX-binding mechanisms, thereby enhancing immune evasion and potentially influencing tissue tropism. The penton base mediates virus internalization via its conserved RGD motif, which engages cellular integrins. Karayan et al. demonstrated that not only mutation of the core RGD sequence (R340E) abolished integrin binding and internalization, but substitution of a neighbouring residue (e.g. W165H) also produced a similarly severe defect, indicating that the RGD motif and its surrounding residues form an integrated functional domain [ 66 ]. Notably, Robinson et al. identified a natural penton base recombinant, HAdV-D60, whose penton base gene was derived from HAdV-D37. In HAdV-D60, the RGD loop was deleted and functionally replaced by a Tyr-Gly-Asp (YGD) motif. Peptide inhibition assays confirmed that this YGD motif mediated integrin binding and enhances corneal inflammation [ 67 ]. In our study, we identified several mutations near the RGD motif in HAdV-7 variants, such as Q338H (HAdV-7 V variants), E320 V (HAdV-7E1 variants), and D325N (most strains of HAdV-7E2 variants) ( Table S1 ). Although these do not alter the RGD sequence itself, they may fine-tune integrin-binding efficiency by modulating the local conformation or electrostatic properties of the functional domain, thereby optimizing viral infectivity under immune or tissue-specific selective pressures. The rate of nucleotide substation found for the HAdV-7 genome was 3.89 × 10 −5 mutations/site/year (95% HPD: 3.05-4.76 × 10 −5 ), comparable to the evolutionary rates calculated by Gonzalez Firth, et al. [ 68 , 69 ]: HAdV-E4 (3.24-3.69 × 10 −5 ), HAdV-C (3.46 × 10 −5 ), and HAdV-B (7.20 × 10 −5 ). However, the nucleotide substitution rates of HAdV-7 hexon gene (1.107 × 10 −3 , 95% HPD: 0.541-0.014 × 10 −3 ) and fibre gene (0.132 × 10 −3 , 95% HPD: 0.283-0.014 × 10 −3 ) calculated by Lin et al. are significantly higher for those for nucleotide substation in entire genome [ 70 ]. This discrepancy may be due to a more limited data set, as only 47 HAdV-7 gene sequences were included in the previous study [ 70 ]. Meanwhile, Firth C, et al [ 69 ] revealed that most dsDNA viruses other than adenoviruses – such as HSV-1, VZV, BK virus, and VARV – exhibit nucleotide substitution rates ranging from 6 × 10 − ⁶ to 8 × 10 − ⁵ mutations/site/year. In contrast, as reported by Jenkins GM, et al [ 71 , 72 ], most RNA viruses – including Dengue virus (types 1–4), Human respiratory syncytial virus (A and B), Foot and mouth disease virus (A, C, O), Avian influenza A virus, Human influenza virus (A and C), Hepatitis E virus, and Norovirus – have nucleotide substitution rates between 0.1 × 10 − ³ and 3.8 × 10 − ³ mutations/site/year. This indicates that dsDNA viruses generally undergo mutations at a lower rate during evolution, which is associated with the higher error propensity of RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) compared to DNA polymerase [ 73 ]. Given this pattern, the slow evolutionary rate of HAdV-7 suggests that its genome remains relatively stable over long periods. Our study reveals that it took approximately 70–80 years for HAdV-7 to evolve into a new variant ( Figure 7 ). Therefore, we predict that the next new variant may emerge around the year 2048. Consequently, U.S. military HAdV-7 vaccines developed based on the 7 V variant are still functional in protection against the prevalent 7E1 and 7E2 variants. These findings hold significant implications for future vaccine development. In conclusion, HAdV-7 is a highly pathogenic virus in children with global distribution, particularly in Asia and North America, which together account for 88.35% of the total reported infections, with China and the United States having the highest numbers. Furthermore, HAdV-7 infections were 3.21 times more prevalent in males (4,484 cases) than in females (1,396 cases), indicating a potential higher susceptibility among males. Moreover, HAdV-7 had a higher CFR (2.41%) than HAdV-4 (0.11%) and constituted the most prevalent genotype (39.28%) among fatalities. This significant finding has been largely overlooked. We also described the molecular evolution characteristics of all catalogued HAdV-7 sequences from 1954 to 2023 to provide a foundational reference for HAdV-7 vaccine design and antiviral drug development. However, we acknowledge certain limitations, such as relying on PubMed as the sole source of published articles, thereby excluding medical literature in other languages. Additionally, due to military confidentiality, data regarding infections and deaths within the military may be biased or underreported. Consequently, the number of HAdV-7 infections, deaths, and the CFR reported in our study may be lower than the actual figures. It should be noted that the extent of this reporting discrepancy is also influenced by a country's level of development, healthcare diagnostic capacity, and public health priorities.
